newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end down 3.04 pct on rating rumours.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end down 3.04 pct on rating rumours.

text.p: Thai stocks ended 3.04 percent lower on Thursday after concerns about the Thai economy and rumours of possible Thai debt ratings prompted local and foreign investors to unload stocks across the board, brokers said.

The SET index retreated 32.14 points to 1,026.54 at the finish on moderate 7.5 billion baht turnover. Declines led advances 349 to 36. The barometer declined to an intra-day low of 1,013.10 in mid-afternoon.
"Investors sold on concerns about local economic problems and on expectations of poor third quarter corporate earnings," said Samart Rusmeerojwong of James Capel Asia.
Finance, bank and electrical components counters lost 6.22, 3.85, and 4.02 percent respectively.
The market was hit by rumours that Thailand's long-term debt ratings may face possible downgrades by Standard & Poor's Corp and Moody's Investors Service.

Finance Minister Bodi Chunnananda later refuted the rumours, saying he had been informed by S&P that the credit rating agency would take four to five months to review its long-term rating on Thailand. Brokers said investors were also worried about the quality of a new government to be formed after November 17 general elections.
"Investors, especially foreigners, fear a new coalition government after the elections will not be as stable as the last one," Samart said.
Nine of the 10 most active stocks were finance companies and banks. Finance One fell 6.50 baht to 95.50, Bangkok Bank lost 10 to 210, and Thai Farmers declined five to 165.
